notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Plates here have blue lettering on white, unlike the black lettering used on the rest of the mainland country.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Plates always begin with the letters ÅL. Since 2011 they carry five digits after the prefix, e.g. ÅL 12345; before that, three letters and 1 to 3 digits.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: This type of plate is shorter than the mainland one, about 390 mm by 130 mm, in a format like ÅBC 123.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Regular plates may use the letters A to Z plus Å, Ä and Ö.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: The international vehicle code was the same as the mainland one until September 2025, when it changed to AX.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: The sole official language is a Scandinavian one rather than the mainland's majority language, so signs lean toward it.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Has its own flag and its own coat of arms, a golden red deer on a blue field.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Web domains end in .ax; phone numbers start +358 18; driving is on the right.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: An archipelago of nearly 300 habitable islands and thousands of skerries, with mostly rocky terrain and thin glacially shaped soil.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Pine trees are common, and low meadows and pastures sit between the rocks.
